claims.text: Phonon-mediated superconductivity governs superconducting behavior in high-entropy alloys.
Lattice distortions and structural disorder enhance electron-phonon interactions in high-entropy alloys.
FCC CoCrFeMnNi is superconducting under the stated conditions.
The CoCrFeMnNi alloy has a face-centered-cubic structure.
STS and EELS can probe phonon dispersion and electron-phonon coupling in the proposed comparison.
Temperatures below 10 K and pressures above 10 GPa enhance superconducting behavior.
Lattice distortion and crystal-structure disorder are the structural mediators of the proposed superconducting response.
Enhanced electron-phonon interactions caused by lattice distortion and disorder increase the superconducting critical temperature.
Under the same conditions, the CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy will have a critical temperature 20% higher than that of a traditional-alloy baseline.
The predicted critical temperature of the high-entropy alloy is 15 K.
The traditional-alloy baseline, exemplified by NbTi, has a critical temperature of 12 K.
The hypothesis is restricted to FCC CoCrFeMnNi under temperatures below 10 K and pressures above 10 GPa.
A measured CoCrFeMnNi critical temperature below 12 K would falsify the hypothesis.
A lack of significant differences in phonon dispersion and electron-phonon coupling between CoCrFeMnNi and the traditional-alloy control would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: A rise from the stated 12 K baseline to 15 K is a 25% increase, not the stated 20% increase; a 20% increase would give 14.4 K.
